BEST RETAINED = BASELINE, unchanged: real 48, insns T116/O116, multiset 4t (target-only +1 b +1 bne, ours-only -1 beq -1 li).

MECHANISM, named and localised. At target 0x48: `bne ->50 / b ->54 / 50: li r30,0 / 54: cmpwi r30,0`; ours collapses this to a single `beq ->54` with the `li` on the fallthrough. The target keeps a redundant branch pair where our build keeps none.

POPULATION FINDING, and this is the part worth carrying forward. The identical signature appears in THREE functions of this one TU: get_vmu_directory at 0x48 (`bne, b` vs our `beq`), writeGauntletSave at 0xe4 (`beq, b` vs our `bne`), and loadGauntletSave at 0x9d4/0x9d8 (the CARDDelete switch's `b ->9dc` plus an unreachable `b ->6c`). Per AGENTS discipline 2 (census before probing any residual seen twice) this should be treated as ONE TU-level question, not three per-function source puzzles. The obvious candidate lever -- global `#pragma peephole off` -- is already MEASURED NEGATIVE on loadGauntletSave (real 885 -> 1096) and is REFUTED, because the same peephole pass also performs the `clrlwi` + `cmplwi` -> `clrlwi.` fusion that the target DOES want. So the target was built with a pass configuration that fuses compares but does NOT eliminate dead/branch-to-next branches. Identifying that configuration is the single highest-value open question in this TU: closing it would move all three functions at once. `#pragma opt_dead_code off` is NOT it (measured folded/no-op).
